_comment: Positive controls. Each entry names a recorded fixture, a mutation applied to its JSON at test time, and the exact problem key that must come out. Mutations touch the JSON half only — the recorded page stays byte-for-byte what lockrot printed, so a check that has stopped producing its own key, or collapsed into `unparsable`, goes red here. Every key a check can emit must appear either here or in `unreachable_by_mutation`, and the test reads those keys out of the check modules' source rather than from a list kept by hand — so a branch nobody poisoned cannot be deleted with the suite still green, which is the hole this tool exists to close, reopened one branch at a time.

libyears left unmeasured with both ends dated
the libyears reported is not the difference between the two dates

unreachable_by_mutation._comment: Problem keys that no mutation of a document can produce, because they are the checks noticing that the PAGE no longer says what it said. A poison only ever changes the JSON — changing the recorded text would make the fixture stop being lockrot's output and would defeat the whole arrangement — so these are reachable only by a real rewording, which is what the corpus run reports as `unparsable`. Declared here with a date so the gap is a line somebody reads rather than a silence.

keys.key: no libyears line in the text at all
keys.why: fires when the header this check reads is gone from the page

keys.key: the composer.lock line is not in a shape this check knows
keys.why: fires when none of the four registered forms of that line matches the page

keys.key: the header both measures libyears and says it did not
keys.why: needs a page carrying both header lines at once, which no renderer produces

keys.key: the text says to migrate to the package itself
keys.why: needs a page carrying the `migrate to` clause; see catalog.MIGRATE_TO, which no target in the 283-pair corpus renders

keys.key: the replacement named in the text is not the one in the JSON
keys.why: the same clause, for the same reason

keys.key: the text calls the lock entry undated, the JSON dates it
keys.why: C2 declines a document with no metadata block, and every one of the 6 pairs whose page reads `· undated` is metadata-less — a lock entry with no date is one the repository never answered for. The branch is kept because nothing guarantees that pairing
